solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trade Union survey of southern European region

parts.note: to survey something is to scan it

explanation.surface: A union commissions a study of a region in southern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Tuscany, the central Italian region around Florence.

clue.text: Floor done afresh in urban attraction

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for urban

parts.note: urban means of the town, so it gives the word town

indicators.note: done afresh means made over again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a city sight whose floor has just been redone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'urban' is an adjective here standing for the noun town; 'afresh' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic fortress by the Thames is one of the capital's major tourist attractions, home of the Crown Jewels.

clue.text: 1/18D is difficult, a bit broken

parts.note: is is shortened to 's, as in it's
difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A London landmark is said to be tough, and partly broken.
explanation.walkthrough: '1/18D' points to the theme: the Shard is the tall glass skyscraper by London Bridge, so the answer also names a London building.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp fragment, a piece broken off glass or pottery.

clue.text: Gone after consuming can? Not such a one

definitions.text: Gone after consuming can? Not such a one

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: someone gone is absent
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone vanished after downing a can of drink, which no teetotaller would do.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: one who abstains would never be gone after a can.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person refrains from alcohol, so drinking a can is exactly what they avoid.

clue.text: Tawdry pap featuring return of violin player

indicators.note: featuring means containing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: pap is an old word for a nipple or teat, as is tit

indicators.note: return means the word for the violin player is read backwards

parts.note: the bow is what plays a violin's strings

explanation.surface: Cheap mushy food served to a returning fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pap' here is the old word for a nipple, not soft food; 'return of' signals the reversal and 'featuring' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is an informal adjective for cheap and inferior, much like tawdry.

clue.text: Western film featuring hard drinker, means of communicating 1/18D

indicators.note: featuring means having within it, so the drinker goes inside

parts.note: a talkie is an old word for a film with sound
an alkie is slang for an alcoholic

explanation.surface: A cowboy film with an alcoholic character becomes a way to talk across London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Walkie-Talkie is the nickname of 20 Fenchurch Street, a London skyscraper, hence '1/18D'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handheld two-way radio lets people speak to each other over a distance.

clue.text: Push the boat

definitions.meaning: to push roughly through a crowd
a flat-bottomed canal or river boat

explanation.surface: An instruction to shove a vessel out.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove one's way forward rudely, and also a long flat-bottomed vessel used on canals.

clue.text: Conductor represented saint and icon

indicators.note: represented means shown again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor depicted as a holy figure in a religious image.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Pipe to enthral with expression of joy

parts.note: to enthral someone is to hook them
ah is a cry of delight

explanation.surface: A pipe that captivates and draws sighs of pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe for smoking, drawing the smoke through a bowl of water.

clue.text: Colourful swimmer swears outrageously

indicators.note: outrageously suggests wild behaviour, so these letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A bright fish curses scandalously.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrasses are brightly coloured reef fish, so a swimmer is a cryptic way to describe one.

clue.text: Outdoor king not finishing cakes — half gone

indicators.note: not finishing means the king's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Alfred the Great was an English king, famous for burning cakes

indicators.note: half gone means the second half of the word for cakes is dropped

parts.note: scones are small baked cakes

explanation.surface: King Alfred leaving his cakes half eaten outside, a nod to the legend that he burnt them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing' cuts ALFRED to ALFRE and 'half gone' cuts SCONES to SCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco means in the open air, as with a meal eaten outside.

clue.text: He gets career working in 1/18D as kitchen helper

indicators.note: working means in operation, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man takes up a job as a kitchen assistant somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cheesegrater is the nickname of the Leadenhall Building in the City of London, hence 'in 1/18D'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a kitchen utensil for shredding cheese, so it helps the cook.

clue.text: Soft left? Right, a bit like Miliband, perhaps

parts.note: Ed Miliband, the former Labour leader, is Ed, so somewhat like him is jokily Ed-dish

explanation.surface: A question about whether a politician resembles the Labour leader once nicknamed Red Ed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led the UK Labour Party and was nicknamed Red Ed; the 'perhaps' admits the coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: Politically left is red, so a soft or mild left-winger is only somewhat red.

clue.text: Diamonds, cards that might prevent flush?

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a pack is a full deck of cards

explanation.surface: Poker talk: diamonds and a deck that might stop someone making a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: The flush is not the poker hand but a reddening of the skin, which a cold compress calms.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of crushed ice held on the skin cools it and stops it reddening or swelling.

clue.text: Make false claim about healthy food

parts.note: to fib is to tell a small lie
re means about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone lies about how wholesome a food is.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage in the diet, from cereals and vegetables, is regarded as good for health.

clue.text: Drinks spiked with something stronger taken by northern freshers?

indicators.note: a drink spiked with something has it added inside

parts.note: beers are drinks

indicators.note: taken by means the spirit is followed by the next letter

parts.note: gin is a spirit, stronger than beer

explanation.surface: Students in the north have their beers laced with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Freshers are British first-year university students, so they are new to it.
explanation.definitionFit: First-year students are novices just starting out, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Found enjoyment right away putting effort in

indicators.note: putting the effort in means placing it inside
away means the letter for right is taken off

parts.note: relish is enjoyment
a stab is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: Someone discovered pleasure instantly by trying hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is the verb meaning set up, not the past of find; 'away' signals the removal and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, a synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: National figure dressed up in a tin bra

indicators.note: dressed up means put into a new outfit, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain's emblem in a metal brassiere, like her armour.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is clothing, a fitting picture for the helmeted figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmeted woman with shield and trident personifies Britain as a nation.

clue.text: Fire setter — everything's incomplete and it's not totally satisfying!

parts.note: to fire something is to light it
the setter refers to the crossword setter, so me

indicators.note: incomplete means the final letter is lost

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: The crossword setter grumbles that nothing is quite finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack or small meal leaves one not completely full.

clue.text: See 1
Sugar-coating report of pop star's confession?

indicators.note: report means what is heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: a pop singer would confess I sing

explanation.surface: A singer's admission is glossed over with flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet coating spread on cakes is made of sugar, and here covers a cake.

clue.text: That lady's man ending up in a pickle in 1/18D

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the final letter moves to the top

parts.note: her means belonging to that lady
a king is a chess man

explanation.surface: A woman's partner gets into trouble somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending up' moves the G of HERKING to the front. The Gherkin is the nickname of 30 St Mary Axe in London, hence 'in 1/18D'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pickled cucumber is a pickle in the sense of a preserved vegetable.

clue.text: Number nurse mixed up for one refusing drugs?

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confused nurse treats a patient who will not take medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not take drugs is not a user of them, the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Horses with no time for antelope

indicators.note: with no means the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a stable is a group of horses owned by one person

explanation.surface: Horses rush past an antelope with no time to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: The sable antelope is a large African antelope with long curved horns.

clue.text: Hero getting in scrape around Virginia

indicators.note: around means the word in wraps the state's letters

parts.note: in is taken as written
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
to hoe is to scrape the soil

explanation.surface: A hero gets into a scrape involving Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece of the wordplay rather than a link word, and 'around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is the hero of Walter Scott's novel of that name.

clue.text: 1/18D chicken crossing road halfway to find big bird

indicators.note: crossing means straddling, so the hen goes around the road's piece

parts.note: a hen is a chicken

indicators.note: halfway means only the first half of the word road

explanation.surface: Why did the chicken cross the road? To find a big bird in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfway' gives RO from road. Heron Tower is a skyscraper in the City of London, hence '1/18D'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herons are large long-legged wading birds.

clue.text: Part of speech I start to teach in Old English — how advanced top set is!

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the letters for Old English

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the word teach

explanation.surface: A teacher explains grammar in Old English to an advanced top set.
explanation.walkthrough: The top set is not a class but the upper teeth, which sit forward of the lower ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper front teeth overlapping the lower ones is how dentists describe this bite.

clue.text: A northern composer lacking drive is socially inadequate type

indicators.note: lacking means the drive letters are removed

parts.note: Antonin Dvorak was a Czech composer
DV is taken as the letters for drive

explanation.surface: A northern composer without ambition is a social misfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops DV from DVORAK, leaving ORAK.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is British slang for an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, after the hooded jacket they wear.

clue.text: Reluctant to embrace sin and drink

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside

parts.note: shy means reluctant
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: Someone shy of sin is wary of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from southern Spain is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Gun law needing new input

indicators.note: input means put in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a canon is a church law

explanation.surface: Firearms legislation needs fresh ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy gun, typically on wheels.
